questions.prompt: When do you usually get up at the weekend?

segments.text: Well, I usually get up around nine at the weekend.
During the week I have to be up at six, so I really enjoy sleeping a bit longer.
On Sundays, for example, I often stay in bed until ten and read the news on my phone. It's my favourite part of the week.
To be honest, I'm a bit of a night owl, so weekends mean a proper lie-in, nine-ish at the earliest.
What I love about it is not hearing the alarm clock after a week of getting up at the crack of dawn.
If I've been out late on Saturday, I've been known to stay in bed until noon, with no regrets whatsoever.

questions.prompt: What do you usually do on Saturday afternoons?

segments.text: On Saturday afternoons I usually meet my friends in the city centre.
We like walking around, having a coffee and sometimes doing a bit of shopping.
Last Saturday, for example, we went to a new café near the river and talked for hours. I really enjoy it because I don't see them much during the week.
Saturday afternoons are usually reserved for my friends. We tend to drift around the old town, pop into a few shops and end up in the same café as always.
It's the perfect way to unwind after a hectic week.
Mind you, if the weather's miserable, we'll just stay in and binge-watch a series instead.

questions.prompt: Would you like to do something different next weekend?

segments.text: Yes, I think I would. I usually stay in the city, so I'd like to go somewhere new.
Maybe I could take a short trip to the mountains or to the coast.
I'd go by train with a friend, and we could walk, take photos and have a nice lunch. I'm sure it would be a good change.
Actually, I've been meaning to get out of the city for ages. If I had more time, I'd drive up to the mountains and spend the whole weekend hiking.
There's nothing like fresh air to clear your head.
Failing that, I'd settle for a day trip to a small village I've never visited.

questions.prompt: Do you live in a house or a flat?

segments.text: I live in a flat in the city centre, on the third floor.
It's quite small, but it has two bedrooms and a nice balcony. I share it with my partner.
The best thing is the location. For example, I can walk to the shops, the metro and my favourite park in just five minutes.
I live in a third-floor flat right in the heart of town. It's not huge, but it's bright and it has a lovely little balcony.
What I like most about it is that everything is on my doorstep: shops, the metro, even a park.
I've been living there for about six years now, and it feels like home.

questions.prompt: What is your favourite room at home, and why?

segments.text: My favourite room is the living room, because it's where we spend most of our time.
It has a big sofa, lots of light and a small shelf with my favourite books.
In the evenings, for example, I like to sit there with a cup of tea and listen to some music. It's very calm and comfortable.
Without a doubt, the living room. It's the heart of the home, and it gets the sun all afternoon, which makes it wonderfully cosy.
What I love about it is the old armchair by the window, which is the perfect spot to curl up with a good book.
I could happily spend whole days there.

questions.prompt: If you could change one thing about your home, what would it be?

segments.text: If I could change one thing, I'd make the kitchen bigger.
At the moment it's really small, so it's difficult to cook when friends come to visit.
For example, last month I invited six people for dinner and we hardly fitted in. A bigger kitchen with a table would be perfect.
If I could wave a magic wand, I'd knock down the wall between the kitchen and the living room.
The kitchen is a bit cramped, and I'd love an open-plan space where I could chat to guests while I'm cooking.
It would make entertaining so much easier, and the whole place would feel twice as big.

questions.prompt: What time do you usually have dinner?

segments.text: We usually have dinner quite late, at about nine o'clock.
I finish work around six, and I often do some shopping or cook something special first.
At the weekend it can be even later. For example, when we go out with friends, we sometimes don't eat until ten or half past.
Around eight, give or take. I'm not a big fan of eating late, as it tends to keep me awake.
During the week we keep it simple, but on Fridays we usually go for a proper meal out.
That's when dinner can stretch on until ten or so, but it's all part of the fun.

questions.prompt: What do you usually do in the evenings?

segments.text: In the evenings I usually relax at home after work.
First I cook dinner, and then I watch a series or talk to my family on the phone.
Sometimes I go for a walk around the neighbourhood, especially when the weather is nice. I try not to do any work after nine, because I want to sleep well.
Once I've switched off from work, I tend to potter around the kitchen and cook something simple.
After that, I'm usually glued to a series or catching up with a friend on the phone.
I've been trying to get into the habit of going for a stroll before bed, as it helps me wind down and sleep like a log.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer staying in or going out in the evening?

segments.text: I prefer staying in on weekdays, but at the weekend I like going out.
After a long day I'm tired and I just want to be comfortable at home.
On Fridays, though, I love meeting friends for dinner or a drink, for example in a small bar near my flat. It's a nice way to start the weekend.
It depends on the day, really. In the week I'm happy to stay in, as I'm usually worn out by the evening.
But come Friday, I'm itching to get out and see people.
There's something about a lively restaurant or a good concert that you just can't get on the sofa, although I wouldn't say no to a quiet night in now and then.

questions.prompt: Do you play any sport or do any exercise?

segments.text: Yes, I go running two or three times a week.
I started last year because I was feeling tired all the time, and now I really enjoy it.
I usually run in the park near my house for about forty minutes. It helps me relax after work, and I sleep much better.
I do, yes. I took up running about a year ago, and I've been hooked ever since.
I'm out three times a week, rain or shine, usually along the river.
What started as a way of shaking off the stress of work has become the highlight of my week, and I feel in far better shape than I did twelve months ago.

questions.prompt: Do you prefer exercising alone or with other people?

segments.text: I prefer exercising with other people, because it's more fun.
When I'm alone, I get bored quickly and sometimes I stop earlier than I planned.
For example, I go to a yoga class with two friends every Tuesday. We help each other to keep going, and afterwards we have a coffee together.
On the whole, I'd say I'm a team player. Exercising with others keeps me motivated, and time just flies.
When I'm on my own, I tend to make excuses and cut the session short.
That said, I do enjoy a solo run now and then, since it gives me a chance to clear my head.

questions.prompt: Is there a sport you'd like to try one day?

segments.text: Yes, I'd really like to try climbing.
I've seen videos of people climbing indoors, and it looks challenging but exciting.
There's a new climbing centre in my city, so I'm thinking of going there next month with a friend. I'm a bit afraid of heights, but I think I'll get used to it.
I've always fancied having a go at climbing. It looks like a great all-round workout, and it's as much about problem-solving as it is about strength.
There's an indoor wall opening nearby, so I might finally take the plunge.
I'm not exactly fearless when it comes to heights, but that's all the more reason to give it a try.

questions.prompt: How much time do you spend on your phone every day?

segments.text: I probably spend about three hours a day on my phone, which is quite a lot.
I use it for messages, social media and the news, and I also check my emails.
For example, I often look at it on the bus and again before bed. I know it's too much, but it's hard to stop.
Embarrassingly, I'm on my phone for about three hours a day, if I'm honest.
A lot of that is work emails and messages, but I do waste time scrolling through social media, too.
I've been trying to cut down lately, but it's easier said than done when it's always within arm's reach.

questions.prompt: What do you usually watch or listen to when you're at home?

segments.text: At home I usually listen to music while I'm cooking or cleaning.
In the evening I like watching series, especially crime dramas and comedies.
For example, I'm watching a Scandinavian detective series at the moment. I also listen to podcasts about history when I'm tidying up the flat.
It varies, but music is always on in the background when I'm pottering about the house.
In the evenings I'm usually hooked on some crime drama or other, the kind where you can't stop at just one episode.
And I've recently got into history podcasts, which are perfect for the washing-up.

questions.prompt: Would you like to spend less time on screens?

segments.text: Yes, I would. I spend too many hours in front of a screen, both at work and at home.
My eyes get tired and I sometimes have a headache in the evening.
So I'd like to read more books and go for more walks. For example, I could put my phone in a drawer after dinner and talk to my family instead.
Definitely. Between work and leisure, I'm glued to a screen for most of my waking hours, and my eyes are paying the price.
If I had more willpower, I'd leave my phone in another room after dinner.
I'd much rather spend that time reading a proper book or chatting face to face, which is what I'd call a real treat.
